extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit arts and humanities organizations and the general public (potential applicants, partners, and stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: General informational page about the Mellon Foundation's mission, examples of funded work, and high-level pointers to its grantmaking areas and process. Not a detailed application guide or eligibility checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission focus: support communities through the arts and humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: Mellon makes grants to support communities through the power of the arts and humanities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Foundation's stated funding purpose; prospective applicants should frame proposals in terms of arts- and humanities‑based community impact and benefits. (Page gives examples via grant stories and news items.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner eligibility: nonprofit organizations aligned with current strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Mellon partners with nonprofit organizations whose work aligns with our current strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies that organizations must demonstrate alignment with the Foundation's active strategies to be considered a partner/grantee; the page links to 'About our grantmaking process' for further details (no specific eligibility rules provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic / geographic focus: consult grantmaking areas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation organizes funding around particular grantmaking areas and highlighted projects (e.g., 'Arts and Humanities Across America'); applicants should consult the specific grantmaking-area pages to determine fit and any area-specific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funded project stories and news as exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: The site presents grant stories and news (e.g., 'The House that Grief Built', 'Colectivo El Ancón de Loíza Incorporado') as examples of supported work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stories function as illustrative examples of the kinds of projects Mellon supports and can guide prospective applicants about scale, scope, and framing; the page itself does not convert these into formal selection criteria.
